description: Reusable editorial quality rubric distilled from public editor interviews and documented workflows. It guides review; it does not imitate or impersonate any editor.

principles.label: Story before style
principles.test: The hook, subject, and payoff are identifiable before decorative treatment.

principles.label: Performance before continuity
principles.test: Filler removal and continuity cleanup must not flatten the strongest delivery.

principles.label: Rhythm is not cut count
principles.test: Pacing is evaluated against the selected profile and protects intentional pauses.

principles.label: B-roll must add meaning
principles.test: Every insert has a visible reason and rights/provenance state.

principles.label: Audience clarity
principles.test: A first-time viewer can follow the intended promise without editor-only context.

principles.label: Reviewable changes
principles.test: Every automated change exposes evidence, timestamp, and an undo path.

principles.label: Sound is story
principles.test: Dialogue, music, room tone, and effects are reviewed as a mix.

principles.label: Delivery is part of editing
principles.test: Captions, safe zones, loudness, codec, and asset rights are checked before export.

principles.label: Fresh eyes
principles.test: The system can compare alternate drafts instead of forcing one template.

principles.label: Editor ergonomics
principles.test: Markers, shortcuts, search, drafts, and recovery reduce cognitive load.

anti_slop_rules: Do not recommend a transition, zoom, SFX, or caption animation without a timestamped reason.
Do not claim quality from a virality score alone.
Do not use one universal cut-rate threshold for every niche or format.
Do not auto-remove pauses that carry emotion, humor, emphasis, or comprehension.
Do not call a project publish-ready when QA is missing or unevaluable.
Do not hide uncertainty; show the evidence and let the editor approve the change.
